Results and open questions

#68. Put 𝑆 =∑𝑛≥21/(𝑛! −1)S=∑n≥21/(n!−1) and 𝐿𝑁 =lcm2≤𝑛≤𝑁⁡(𝑛! −1)LN=lcm2≤n≤N⁡(n!−1). Any rational 𝑆 =𝑎/𝑞S=a/q with 𝑞 >0q>0 satisfies the two incomparable exclusions 𝑞 ∤299999!q∤299999! and 𝑞 ≥239990 >1012038q≥239990>1012038. The first is a factorial divisibility constraint from a fresh exact GMP carry census through 𝑚 =300000m=300000 together with a Lean consumer; that replay matches the previously retained certificate, while an independent replay through 40004000 reproduces the unit-carry prefix. The second is an independent continued-fraction size bound. Neither implication yields the other, and neither proves irrationality. The paper and Lean proof give lim inflog⁡𝐿𝑁/(𝑁3/2log⁡𝑁) ≥2√2/3lim inflog⁡LN/(N3/2log⁡N)≥22/3. This is a common-denominator theorem: it shows why clearing every summand separately cannot make the positive tail small, but says nothing by itself about the denominator after cancellation. Lean separately checks that irrationality of 𝑆S is equivalent to cofinally many non-unit factorial carries, and checks a finite quotient-band channel obstruction. The required cofinal carries are not produced. A local exact calculation at the prime 1248712487 exhibits two critical roots for gap 1212, so the earlier small-prime pattern of at most one critical root is not a uniform theorem; those roots have factorial values 442442 and 63006300, not 11. Lean checks the 3/23/2 theorem as common_denominator_growth_liminf in PaperCompleteLiminf.lean. The separate public Lean release wcook04/plectis-erdos-lean states the 3/23/2 bound at commit 52f29ad1 as common_denominator_growth in its entry PalomarCorpus/E68 and proves it; that repository’s Linux replay of Palomar’s Comparator stage accepted the entry with both kernels (run 34782407633).

Problem 0.1 (Erdős #68). Is

𝑆=∑𝑛≥21𝑛!−1S=∑n≥21n!−1

irrational?

The denominator exclusions

The factorial-divisibility exclusion.

For 𝑚 ≥2m≥2, put

𝐻𝑚=𝑚∑𝑛=21𝑛!−1,𝑍𝑚=⌊𝑚!𝐻𝑚⌋+1,Hm=∑n=2m1n!−1,Zm=⌊m!Hm⌋+1,

and for 𝑚 ≥3m≥3 define the carry

𝑏𝑚=𝑚𝑍𝑚−1+1−𝑍𝑚.bm=mZm−1+1−Zm.

Here 𝑍𝑚Zm is the least integer strictly greater than 𝑚!𝐻𝑚m!Hm, even when 𝑚!𝐻𝑚m!Hm is itself an integer; it is not always ⌈𝑚!𝐻𝑚⌉⌈m!Hm⌉. Thus 𝑏𝑚 =1bm=1 means that the next integers scale exactly by the factor 𝑚m: 𝑍𝑚 =𝑚𝑍𝑚−1Zm=mZm−1. The exclusion rests on the implication, for integers 𝑎a and 𝑞 >0q>0,

𝑆=𝑎/𝑞,𝑞∣(𝑚−1)!,𝑚≥3⟹𝑏𝑚=1.(1)(1)S=a/q,q∣(m−1)!,m≥3⟹bm=1.

For 𝑛 ≥3n≥3, we have 1/(𝑛! −1) <(𝑛 −1)/𝑛!1/(n!−1)<(n−1)/n! and ∑𝑛>𝑚(𝑛 −1)/𝑛! =1/𝑚!∑n>m(n−1)/n!=1/m!, so 0 <𝑚!(𝑆 −𝐻𝑚) <10<m!(S−Hm)<1. Under the divisibility hypothesis, 𝑚!𝑆m!S is integral, so this bound identifies it as 𝑍𝑚Zm. The same argument at 𝑚 −1m−1 gives 𝑍𝑚 =𝑚!𝑆 =𝑚𝑍𝑚−1Zm=m!S=mZm−1, proving eq:finite-denominator-consumer. Thus 𝑏𝑚 ≠1bm≠1 forces every rational denominator to be at least 𝑚m, since any smaller positive 𝑞q would divide (𝑚 −1)!(m−1)!. The recorded exact value 𝑏300000 ≠1b300000≠1 therefore excludes every divisor of 299999!299999! as a denominator of 𝑆S. This does not exclude every 299999299999-smooth denominator: sufficiently high powers of a small prime need not divide 299999!299999!. Section 7 distinguishes this reported full run from the smaller computation repeated in the rewrite notes.

The size exclusion.

For the continued-fraction calculation, put 𝐵 =280000B=280000 and let 𝑁N be the first integer with 𝑁! −1 >𝐵N!−1>B. Define

ℓ=𝑁−1∑𝑛=2⌊𝐵𝑛!−1⌋,𝑢=ℓ+(𝑁−2)+⌊2𝐵𝑁!−1⌋+1.ℓ=∑n=2N−1⌊Bn!−1⌋,u=ℓ+(N−2)+⌊2BN!−1⌋+1.

Rounding the 𝑁 −2N−2 prefix terms down loses less than 𝑁 −2N−2. Successive terms in the omitted tail have ratio less than 1/(𝑁 +1)1/(N+1), so their sum is less than (𝑁 +1)/(𝑁(𝑁! −1)) <2/(𝑁! −1)(N+1)/(N(N!−1))<2/(N!−1). Thus ℓ/𝐵 <𝑆 <𝑢/𝐵ℓ/B<S<u/B. Exact integer computation gives 𝑁 =7054N=7054 and 𝑢 −ℓ =7053u−ℓ=7053.

Apply the continued-fraction algorithm to both endpoints. Retain a common integer part only while both remainders are nonzero, then invert and reverse the endpoint order. The computation gives 2344923449 common partial quotients 𝑎0,…,𝑎23448a0,…,a23448. Their convergent denominators satisfy

𝑄−2=1,𝑄−1=0,𝑄𝑗=𝑎𝑗𝑄𝑗−1+𝑄𝑗−2,𝑄23448≥239990.Q−2=1,Q−1=0,Qj=ajQj−1+Qj−2,Q23448≥239990.

Every rational in the open enclosure has this initial segment. To see why it gives a denominator bound, write 𝑃𝑗/𝑄𝑗Pj/Qj for the last common convergent, with 𝑗 =23448j=23448. A continuation with complete quotient 𝑥/𝑦 >1x/y>1, where 𝑥,𝑦x,y are coprime positive integers, has reduced denominator 𝑄𝑗𝑥 +𝑄𝑗−1𝑦 ≥𝑄𝑗Qjx+Qj−1y≥Qj; if the expansion terminates at this convergent, its denominator is 𝑄𝑗Qj. Reducedness follows from the determinant identity 𝑃𝑗𝑄𝑗−1 −𝑃𝑗−1𝑄𝑗 = ±1PjQj−1−Pj−1Qj=±1 . The integer comparison 239990 >1012038239990>1012038 completes the second exclusion. A non-reduced representation has a denominator at least as large as the reduced one, so the bound applies to every 𝑞q in 𝑆 =𝑎/𝑞S=a/q. The long record gives the immutable program and receipt links.

Neither restriction implies the other: the prime 300007300007 satisfies the divisibility restriction and fails the size restriction, whereas 299999!299999! does the reverse. Both conclusions are finite; they do not decide the irrationality question posed by Erdős [1] and listed in Bloom’s catalogue [2]. Their computational certificates are specified in §7.

The corresponding rationality criterion.

A finite non-unit carry excludes particular denominators. Non-unit carries at arbitrarily large indices are equivalent to irrationality.

Theorem 1.1 (exact carry characterisation). The following conditions are equivalent:

𝑆∉ℚ,(∀𝐵)(∃𝑚>𝐵) 𝑏𝑚≠1,(∀𝐵)(∃𝑚>𝐵) 𝑚∤𝑍𝑚.S∉Q,(∀B)(∃m>B) bm≠1,(∀B)(∃m>B) m∤Zm.

In particular, cofinal non-unit carries imply irrationality; equivalently, the original problem is the criterion using the next integer.

Lean: carry characterisation.

Proof. Rationality forces eventual unit carries by eq:finite-denominator-consumer. Conversely, if 𝑏𝑚 =1bm=1 eventually, then 𝑍𝑚/𝑚!Zm/m! is eventually constant. Since

𝐻𝑚<𝑍𝑚/𝑚!≤𝐻𝑚+1/𝑚!,Hm<Zm/m!≤Hm+1/m!,

that rational constant is 𝑆S. Finally writing 𝑥 =(𝑚 −1)!𝐻𝑚−1x=(m−1)!Hm−1 gives 𝑏𝑚 =𝑚 −1 −⌊𝑚{𝑥} +1/(𝑚! −1)⌋bm=m−1−⌊m{x}+1/(m!−1)⌋, hence −1 ≤𝑏𝑚 ≤𝑚 −1−1≤bm≤m−1. For 𝑚 ≥3m≥3, these bounds together with 𝑍𝑚 =𝑚𝑍𝑚−1 +1 −𝑏𝑚Zm=mZm−1+1−bm imply 𝑚 ∣𝑍𝑚m∣Zm exactly when 𝑏𝑚 =1bm=1. ◻

For 𝑒e, multiplication by 𝑚!m! clears every denominator of the partial sum; here gcd(𝑚!,𝑚! −1) =1gcd(m!,m!−1)=1 prevents even the last summand from being cleared when 𝑚 ≥3m≥3. For the tail arguments below, the issue is the gap to an integer after scaling, not just the size of the unscaled tail. The remaining sections study that gap and the exact coefficient equations. Appendix A gives a factorial-digit formulation and the floor correction relating the two sequences. Secondary constructions are proved in the long companion paper, Denominators and Rationality Criteria.

Integer vectors for cancelling weighted sums

For a chosen integer 𝐷 ≥2D≥2, we seek integer coefficients whose contributions at denominators 2! −1,…,𝐷! −12!−1,…,D!−1 vanish, removing the first few terms of a remainder. To construct such coefficients, we remove powers of 𝑑!d! from 𝑛!n!. For example, at 𝑑 =3d=3 and 𝑛 =4n=4, removing the factor 3! =63!=6 leaves 44, and 24/5 −4/5 =424/5−4/5=4: the fractional part is unchanged. For a finitely supported integer vector 𝜆 =(𝜆𝑛)𝑛≥1λ=(λn)n≥1 and an integer 𝑑 ≥2d≥2, define

𝑊𝑑,𝑛=𝑛!(𝑑!)⌊𝑛/𝑑⌋,𝑀(𝜆)=∑𝑛𝜆𝑛𝑛!,𝑉𝑑(𝜆)=∑𝑛𝜆𝑛𝑊𝑑,𝑛.Wd,n=n!(d!)⌊n/d⌋,M(λ)=∑nλnn!,Vd(λ)=∑nλnWd,n.

The weights are integers. Indeed, write 𝑛 =𝑘𝑑 +𝑟n=kd+r with 0 ≤𝑟 <𝑑0≤r<d. The quotient 𝑛!/((𝑑!)𝑘𝑟!)n!/((d!)kr!) is a multinomial coefficient, and 𝑊𝑑,𝑛Wd,n is 𝑟!r! times that integer. Since 𝑛! =(𝑑!)⌊𝑛/𝑑⌋𝑊𝑑,𝑛n!=(d!)⌊n/d⌋Wd,n and 𝑑! ≡1(mod𝑑! −1)d!≡1(modd!−1), the difference (𝑛! −𝑊𝑑,𝑛)/(𝑑! −1)(n!−Wd,n)/(d!−1) is an integer. Thus the same fractional-part calculation holds for every 𝑑 ≥2d≥2 and 𝑛 ≥1n≥1. Write 𝑒𝑛en for the vector with coefficient 11 at index 𝑛n and 00 elsewhere. We temporarily allow index 11 to simplify the basis calculation; we later require its coefficient to vanish. This does not add the undefined term 1/(1! −1)1/(1!−1) to 𝑆S.

The exponent ⌊𝑛/𝑑⌋⌊n/d⌋ is chosen for its changes at multiples of 𝑑d, not to remove the largest power of 𝑑!d! dividing 𝑛!n!. Consequently, the adjacent differences below affect only sums with 𝑑 ∣𝑛d∣n. Call 𝑀(𝜆)M(λ) the moment, without assuming it positive. The remainder

R(𝜆)=∑𝑑≥2𝑉𝑑(𝜆)𝑑!−1R(λ)=∑d≥2Vd(λ)d!−1

R(𝜆)−𝑀(𝜆)𝑆=𝑁∑𝑑=2𝑉𝑑(𝜆)−𝑀(𝜆)𝑑!−1∈ℤ.R(λ)−M(λ)S=∑d=2NVd(λ)−M(λ)d!−1∈Z.

𝑉𝑑(𝑇𝑛)=(𝑑!−1)𝑊𝑑,𝑛𝟏𝑑∣𝑛.Vd(Tn)=(d!−1)Wd,n1d∣n.

The support restriction and the remainder

Fix 𝐷 ≥2D≥2 and write

𝐿𝐷=lcm2≤𝑑≤𝐷⁡(𝑑!−1),𝐾𝐷=𝐿𝐷𝑒1−𝐷∑𝑑=2𝐿𝐷𝑑!−1𝑈𝑑.LD=lcm2≤d≤D⁡(d!−1),KD=LDe1−∑d=2DLDd!−1Ud.

𝑉𝑑(𝜆)≡𝑀(𝜆)(mod𝑑!−1).(4)(4)Vd(λ)≡M(λ)(modd!−1).

R(𝑡𝐾𝐷+∑𝑛>𝐷𝑧𝑛𝑈𝑛)=𝑡𝐿𝐷(𝑆−𝐻𝐷)+∑𝑛>𝐷𝑧𝑛.(6)(6)R(tKD+∑n>DznUn)=tLD(S−HD)+∑n>Dzn.

The finite integer-difference identity shows that changing coefficients at fixed moment preserves the fractional part. A nonintegral remainder rules out 𝑆 =𝑎/𝑞S=a/q when 𝑞 ∣𝑀q∣M. To exclude every denominator this way, each positive integer 𝑞q must divide the moment of some nonintegral remainder in the family; unbounded moments alone do not guarantee this.

Let 𝑎𝐷aD and 𝑢𝑛un be the coefficients at index 11 of 𝐾𝐷KD and 𝑈𝑛Un, respectively. Requiring that coefficient to vanish gives

𝑡𝑎𝐷+∑𝑛>𝐷𝑧𝑛𝑢𝑛=0.(7)(7)taD+∑n>Dznun=0.

Consequently the attainable moments are

𝐿𝐷𝑔𝐷gcd(𝑔𝐷,𝑎𝐷)ℤ,𝑔𝐷=gcd{𝑢𝑛:𝑛>𝐷}.(8)(8)LDgDgcd(gD,aD)Z,gD=gcd{un:n>D}.

Indeed, finite integer combinations of the 𝑢𝑛un form 𝑔𝐷ℤgDZ. The positive generator is attained because a gcd of any integer family is a finite integer combination of its members. An attaining vector is primitive: division by a common coefficient factor greater than one would preserve all zero weighted sums and produce a smaller positive moment. For odd 𝑛n, 𝑢𝑛 =0un=0 by induction. For a prime 𝑝p, the sole nonzero proper-divisor contribution at 2𝑝2p gives 𝑢2𝑝 = −2(2𝑝)!/2𝑝 ≠0u2p=−2(2p)!/2p≠0. Every tail thus contains a nonzero coefficient, so 𝑔𝐷 >0gD>0.

Computing the gcd from finitely many coefficients.

The scalar recurrence is

𝑢2=2,𝑢𝑛=−∑𝑑∣𝑛2≤𝑑<𝑛𝑊𝑑,𝑛𝑢𝑑(𝑛>2).u2=2,un=−∑d∣n2≤d<nWd,nud(n>2).

To prove that an integer 𝑔g divides every 𝑢𝑛un with 𝑛 >𝐷n>D, use induction in this recurrence. Once the terms with 𝐷 <𝑑 <𝑛D<d<n are divisible by 𝑔g, only 𝑑 ≤𝐷d≤D need further consideration. For these terms we use

𝑘!∣𝑊𝑑,𝑑𝑘=(𝑑𝑘)!(𝑑!)𝑘.k!∣Wd,dk=(dk)!(d!)k.

The quotient by 𝑘!k! counts partitions into 𝑘k unordered blocks of size 𝑑d.

Theorem 2.2 (a finite formula for the gcd). Choose a prime ℓℓ with 𝐷/2 <ℓ ≤𝐷D/2<ℓ≤D and put 𝐻 =𝐷(2ℓ −1)H=D(2ℓ−1). Then

𝑔𝐷=gcd(𝑢𝐷+1,…,𝑢𝐻),𝐻<2𝐷2.gD=gcd(uD+1,…,uH),H<2D2.

Proof. Since 𝐷 <2ℓ ≤𝐷(2ℓ −1) =𝐻D<2ℓ≤D(2ℓ−1)=H, the finite interval includes the nonzero term 𝑢2ℓ = −(2ℓ)!/2ℓ−1u2ℓ=−(2ℓ)!/2ℓ−1. Thus its gcd 𝑔g is positive and 𝑔 ∣(2ℓ)!g∣(2ℓ)!. For 𝑛 >𝐻n>H and a divisor 𝑑 ≤𝐷d≤D, the integer 𝑛/𝑑n/d is at least 2ℓ2ℓ. The equal-block divisibility above gives 𝑔 ∣(𝑛/𝑑)! ∣𝑊𝑑,𝑛g∣(n/d)!∣Wd,n. Every term of the recurrence with 𝑑 ≤𝐷d≤D is therefore divisible by 𝑔g. Strong induction handles the remaining divisors 𝐷 <𝑑 <𝑛D<d<n, whose coefficients are already divisible by 𝑔g. Thus 𝑔g divides the entire tail. Finally 𝐻 ≤𝐷(2𝐷 −1) <2𝐷2H≤D(2D−1)<2D2.

Remark. It remains to prove that the displayed congruence fails at arbitrarily large indices for this particular 𝐶C. Any one finite list of failures, however long, is not enough. The theorem is an equivalence, not an estimate for the distribution of these residues.

When subtracting the tail changes a floor

The digit uses 𝐶C, but the carry uses a partial sum. Their floors can differ when the omitted tail crosses an integer. Write {𝑥} =𝑥 −⌊𝑥⌋{x}=x−⌊x⌋ for the fractional part and 𝟏1 for an indicator, and put

𝛿𝑚=𝑚!∑𝑛>𝑚1𝑛!(𝑛!−1),𝜎𝑚=𝟏{{𝑚!𝐶}<𝛿𝑚}.δm=m!∑n>m1n!(n!−1),σm=1{{m!C}<δm}.

Since 0 <𝛿𝑚 <1/((𝑚 +1)! −1) <10<δm<1/((m+1)!−1)<1 by comparison with 𝑚!∑𝑛>𝑚1/𝑛! <1m!∑n>m1/n!<1, subtracting this tail lowers a floor by exactly 𝜎𝑚σm. Hence

𝑍𝑚=𝑚!𝑚∑𝑛=21𝑛!+⌊𝑚!𝐶⌋+1−𝜎𝑚.Zm=m!∑n=2m1n!+⌊m!C⌋+1−σm.

The first term is an integer, and its difference from 𝑚m times the preceding one is 11. Substitution in the definition of 𝑏𝑚bm therefore gives, for 𝑚 ≥3m≥3,

𝑏𝑚=𝑚−1−𝑑𝑚(𝐶)+𝜎𝑚−𝑚𝜎𝑚−1.(18)(18)bm=m−1−dm(C)+σm−mσm−1.

Equality {𝑚!𝐶} =𝛿𝑚{m!C}=δm leaves an integral prefix and gives no correction. A fractional part smaller than the tail crosses an integer, however small the tail is; neither indicator can simply be omitted.

What the source records establish.

The identities for adjacent coefficient differences, the recursion that isolates one weighted sum, the vanishing moment, the individual values 𝑉𝑑Vd, and the factor 1212 have formal proofs in the integer basis for the weighted sums. The unique integral basis expansion, attainable-moment formula and construction on an arithmetic progression are ordinary proofs, described in the integer basis for the weighted sums and, for the grid construction, in the primitive vector on an arithmetic progression. The quadratic stopping theorem is checked in the quadratic stopping bound for the gcd, together with the scalar recurrence, the equal-block divisibility and the explicit coefficient at twice a prime used in its proof. The divisibility lcm⁡(1,…,𝑛) ∣𝑢𝑛lcm⁡(1,…,n)∣un and the depth-44 moment 13801380 have ordinary proofs with exact checks in exact checks of the moment divisibility. Checks for the finite gcd calculation are in the finite gcd verification script. The inherited generic lemmas in gcd lemmas with an assumed divisibility assume that divisibility; they do not prove it for the factorial coefficients. The growth liminf is the ordinary asymptotic consequence of the finite terminal-block inequality cited above, and Lean checks it as the liminf bound for the common denominator. The checked counterpart of the growth liminf in the public Lean release wcook04/plectis-erdos-lean at commit 52f29ad1 is identified in the next source paragraph for (10).

Formal proof checking does not assess external novelty or the significance of the remaining hypothesis. The complete source register, receipts and failed-route calculations belong to the long record.

Formal sources for the common-denominator bound.

The formal sources for (10) include the liminf bound for the common denominator. The separate public Lean release wcook04/plectis-erdos-lean at commit 52f29ad1 states the bound (10), with the least common multiple of 𝑛! −1n!−1 over 2 ≤𝑛 ≤𝑁2≤n≤N as the common denominator, as common_denominator_growth and in extended real form as common_denominator_growth_liminf. The statements are in the Comparator challenge file PalomarCorpus/E68/Challenge.lean, where the proofs are left as sorry. The solution file Solutions/PalomarCorpus/E68/CommonDenominatorGrowth.lean closes both by transfer from common_denominator_growth in ErdosProblems/Erdos68/PaperCompleteAsymptotics.lean and common_denominator_growth_liminf in ErdosProblems/Erdos68/PaperCompleteLiminf.lean of the same release. The supplied release record reports that a Linux replay of Palomar’s Comparator stage accepted the entry with the Lean kernel and with NanoDa (run 34782407633). This bound concerns a common denominator of the partial sums. It is not a lower bound for the denominator of the series under a rationality assumption. The finite-block inequality has a separate Lean source, the inequality for a terminal block.

Related denominator estimates.

Shared prime-power divisibility was used to control the spacing of factorial indices by Erdős and Stewart [13]. The subtraction in the proof of (10) is the case 𝑃 = −1P=−1 of Luca and Shparlinski’s polynomial-shift argument [9], also used by Lai . These sources supply that subtraction, not the lcm asymptotic stated here. The extension to a fixed nonzero polynomial shift 𝑛! +𝑃(𝑛)n!+P(n) uses an eventual cutoff for positivity and nonvanishing [8], attributed there to Luca and Shparlinski . Its proof, including the uniform choice of cutoff and the lower-order gcd loss, is in the long record, §2. The non-polynomial shift 𝑛! +2𝑛 −1n!+2n−1 uses a different, three-index elimination [14]; it is not an instance of that extension. Spacing methods for factorial congruences and the fixed-value multiplicity bound [17] are relevant comparisons, not ingredients of this proof.

Comparison with denominator savings in 𝑝p-adic linear forms.

A related denominator-saving argument occurs in work of Lai, Lupu and Sprang on linear forms in 𝑝p-adic zeta values. Here 𝑝 ≥5p≥5 is a fixed prime and 𝑛n indexes the forms. They save a product Φ𝑛Φn of prime powers from coefficient-denominator bounds built from lcm⁡(1,…,𝑛)lcm⁡(1,…,n) . Its growth rate [10] enters their inequality [10] and irrationality criterion , quoted from Lai [11]. On the same unbounded subsequence, nonzero forms with integer coefficients must have their 𝑝p-adic absolute values, multiplied by the largest ordinary absolute value of a coefficient, tending to zero. For 𝐻𝑀HM, the analogous saving is 𝐿𝑀/den⁡(𝐻𝑀)LM/den⁡(HM), whose required asymptotic size is not established here. This is a comparison of denominator control; no 𝑝p-adic theorem is applied to 𝑆S.

Factorial-series comparisons.

Galambos treats the rationality of Cantor series in . Koepf and Schmersau prove irrationality for nonterminating factorial expansions whose digits are not eventually maximal [5]. Appendix A specifies the canonical convention and proves the criterion for 𝐶 =𝑆 −𝑒 +2C=S−e+2 directly.

The argument in §1 identifies the next integer above a scaled partial sum. This differs from the factorial-tail integrality lemma of Hančl and Tijdeman [6]: 𝑚!𝐻𝑚m!Hm need not be integral; under the denominator-divisibility hypothesis, it is 𝑚!𝑆m!S that is integral. The exclusion can also be expressed by saying that the least positive 𝑟r with 𝑞 ∣𝑟!q∣r! is at least 300000300000. Sondow uses this factorial index for 𝑒e [15]; his approximation bound is not applied to 𝑆S.

For integer-coefficient factorial series, Hančl and Tijdeman prove integrality of normalised rational tails [6], and classify the polynomial-coefficient case [6]. The long record, Appendix B.2, explains the direct application after rewriting 𝑆S as a factorial series with integer carry-defect coefficients. These results do not remove the indicators in (18).

Selected-prime and mean comparisons.

The test with an additional selected prime adds (2𝑝 +1)𝐶𝑝𝑞 <2𝑝2(2𝑝 −1)!(2p+1)Cpq<2p2(2p−1)! for a prime 𝑞 ∣𝑅𝑝q∣Rp to (12). The long paper, §4, constructs blocks with 𝑞 ∣𝑅𝑝q∣Rp and proves the equivalence with the two inequalities. This is an additional restriction, not an equivalent criterion for irrationality. Its §7 gives a sufficient joint mean bound for (13), on the same sets of parameters for both summands; separate estimates on unrelated sets do not suffice.

Additional proofs and comparison files.

A related cofactor construction gives a remainder equal to a determinant times 𝑆S, up to an integer. For a positive starting parameter, its primitive normalization is the progression vector of §3.2, up to sign; the long record, §7, proves this identification. Nonintegrality along the family with least support index tending to infinity is equivalent to irrationality, not a condition established by the construction.

The interval condition at the lower endpoint and the test for 𝑝2 ∣𝑍2𝑝p2∣Z2p combine quantities at the same index. Non-unit carries at arbitrarily large 2𝑝2p, with 𝑝p an odd prime, already suffice without that test. These comparisons, the condition for two consecutive unit carries, and an example distinguishing the integer recurrence from its defining floor relation are given in the long record. It also explains why any fixed collection of denominator factors eventually divides the factorial being removed.

The standalone formal source for the carry equivalences is the isolated source for the next-integer criterion. The module on factorial-scaled partial sums and the next integer duplicates this development; it is not the standalone source. Formal proofs of the rationality equivalence are given in rationality and factorial residues. Its statements corresponding to the paper are eventual residue congruence under rationality and arbitrarily late failures of the residue congruence. The combined statement the full factorial-residue equivalence corresponds to Theorem A.1 and the following remark. The long record also gives the two simultaneous inequalities for a selected prime, the shared-factor bound for the selected factors, and the eventual absorption of fixed denominator indices. The separate public Lean release wcook04/plectis-erdos-lean at commit 52f29ad1 selects those three endpoints as movingPrivateFactorScaleSplit_implies_irrational, splitFactorNormalizedCollision_implies_irrational and fixedOwnerPair_eventually_absorbed in PalomarCorpus/E68/Challenge.lean. These three release statements are separate from the historical public links above. The supplied release record reports acceptance of the E68 entry at commit 52f29ad1 by the Linux replay of Palomar’s Comparator stage (run 34782407633, cited earlier in this appendix). That report does not establish a new compilation of every source linked by this manuscript. The unconditional correction (18) is checked in the exact floor correction for the companion series, and the pole-residue identity and the two displayed reciprocal equalities are checked in the prime-power noncancellation criterion. The complete maximal-hit data come from the separate exact modular scan; the carry census and continued-fraction certificate use exact integer computation outside Lean. What is checked in Lean
  • The exact integral normal form: the series is irrational if and only if the strict factorial successor 𝑍𝑚Zm misses divisibility by m cofinally.
  • The equivalent carry form: rationality is equivalent to eventual unit carry, so cofinally many non-unit carries imply irrationality.
  • Canonical factorial digits, exact remainder recurrences, zero-tail propagation, and the divisor-factorial centre recurrence.
  • Integral channel congruences, the lcm tax, the prime unit translator, and factorial-grid Cramer residual identities.
  • Weighted projection and factor-split rigidity consumers with their exact modular and Archimedean hypotheses.
  • The zero-plateau and first-exit carry dichotomy, prime-power prefix obstructions, and exact doubled-prime branch characterisations.
  • A Lean-checked implication from one exact non-unit carry to a rational-denominator lower bound; a fresh exact GMP certificate at 𝑚 =300000m=300000 supplies the finite input used by the papers; the event-trace and unit carries match the previously retained receipt.
What is not checked
  • Irrationality of the factorial-denominator series.
  • A theorem producing cofinally many divisibility misses or non-unit carries.
  • Cofinal strict nonintegrality of the factorial-grid Cramer residual.
  • The weighted collision-product and complementary-residue estimates needed by the factor-split projection consumer.
  • The GMP computation is an exact finite external certificate, not a Lean evaluation and not an unbounded argument.
The formal record: 2 main results, 5 open obligations, 13 Lean modules, finite search evidence, Comparator review

Open obligations

Prove any one of these and the corresponding reduction above becomes unconditional.

  • weighted_collision_and_complementary_residue On an unbounded family of tailored prime blocks, prove both the weighted collision-core product bound and the independent complementary-residue inequality consumed by the exact unit-factor scale split.
  • cofinal_prime_power_amplification At infinitely many genuinely nonterminal indices, prove quantitative repeated-support valuation amplification strong enough to meet the checked endpoint inequality.
  • cofinal_lower_endpoint_escape For infinitely many primes, force the reduced predecessor gap outside the exact lower unit-carry cylinder.
  • cofinal_doubled_prime_branch_failure For infinitely many odd primes, rule out both exact p2-divisibility branches at index 2p by coupling the carry value to the predecessor residue.
  • cramer_residual_nonintegrality Construct an unbounded factorial-grid family whose exact Cramer residual is nonintegral, using a determinant, valuation, cancellation, or gcd-of-minors certificate that controls the finite sign-changing block.

Finite search evidence

A retained exact GMP receipt through 𝑚 =300000m=300000 records a non-unit carry at that index, so every positive rational denominator satisfies q ∤ 299999!.299999!. A byte-identical regeneration of that receipt with the current driver is outstanding in this revision; a separate exact replay through 4000 reproduces the unit-carry prefix. The Lean consumer turns one non-unit carry at m into 𝑞 ≥𝑚q≥m; it does not prove a cofinal statement. An independent continued-fraction enclosure gives 𝑞 ≥239990q≥239990. At the prime 12487 and gap 12, exact polynomial arithmetic exhibits two critical roots 4626 and 7848, so the small-prime pattern of at most one critical root is not uniform; those roots have factorial values 442 and 6300, not 1.
